# CalendarView

Header: `winui/ui/datetime/CalendarView.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/datetime/CalendarView.hpp`.

A month calendar: the days of one month in a grid of weeks, with the month's name above them and buttons to page through months.

Clicking a day selects it, and clicking a selected day removes it from the selection. Clicking the heading zooms out to the months of the year and then to the years of the decade, and clicking a month or a year zooms back in. The days of the neighboring months fill the first and last weeks, in a dimmed color when [`out_of_scope_enabled`](#out_of_scope_enabled) is true.

The names of the months and the days and the first day of the week come from [regional_date_format()](../core/namespace-ui.md#regional_date_format) unless the calendar sets its own.

Keyboard: the arrow keys move between days, Home and End go to the first and the last day of the month, PageUp and PageDown move by a month, Ctrl+Up zooms out and Ctrl+Down zooms in, and Enter or Space select the focused day or zoom into the focused month or year. The heading, the two paging buttons and the grid are four tab stops.

[`ui::CalendarView`](#uicalendarview) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::CalendarViewControl calendar;
calendar.set_selection_mode(ui::CalendarViewSelectionMode::Multiple);
calendar.on_selected_dates_changed([](const std::vector<std::chrono::year_month_day>& dates)
                                   { std::printf("%zu days picked\n", dates.size()); });
```

## `ui::CalendarView`

The declarative form of [CalendarViewControl](#uicalendarviewcontrol): a month calendar.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::vector<std::chrono::year_month_day>> picked;

window.set_content(ui::CalendarView{
    .selected_dates      = picked,
    .group_label_visible = true,
    .is_blackout         = [](std::chrono::year_month_day date)
    {
        const std::chrono::weekday day{std::chrono::sys_days{date}};
        return day == std::chrono::Saturday || day == std::chrono::Sunday; // weekdays only
    },
});
```

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Call `visit` once for each child this element owns, in order (back to front where they overlap). The one override a container needs beyond measure, arrange and render. The default of every tree-wide walk recurses through it ([collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables), the popup walk, clear_dirty(), [build_visual_tree()](../tree/element.md#build_visual_tree), sync_composition(), [sync_native()](../tree/element.md#sync_native), [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) and [automation_children()](#automation_children)), so a custom container that lists its children here gets focus, popups, dirty clearing, ticks, composition, native controls and automation right without forwarding any of them. Default: no children, a leaf.

List the children the walks should reach, normally every one this element owns. A walk that must see a different set overrides that walk alone: a composite that is one tab stop and one automation node, a split view leaving its closed pane out of focus and popups. A control that parks parts (an unselected page, a hidden button) may leave them out here instead and clear them in [clear_dirty_override()](../tree/element.md#clear_dirty_override) (and tick them in [tick_override()](#tick_override)), so a parked part never stays dirty.

Const so the const walks can use it, though it hands out mutable children: they are owned objects of their own, not part of this element's state. A tick can run a handler that adds or removes children, so a container that allows that walks its list by index.

Example: 
```cpp
class Row : public ui::Element
{
    void for_each_child(ui::ChildVisitor visit) const override
    {
        for (const auto& child : children_)
        {
            visit(*child);
        }
    }

    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ui::Element>> children_;
};
```

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children an automation client sees under this node, immediate children only. A client walks the tree one level at a time, and the parent comes from [parent()](../tree/element.md#parent). Defaults to every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists. Override it only to show a client something else: the children in a different order, or without parts that are only decoration. A composite that is one automation node lists nothing.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp

```

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

This element's own part of [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## Enumerations

### CalendarViewSelectionMode

```cpp
enum class CalendarViewSelectionMode
```

How many dates a [CalendarView](#uicalendarview) lets the user select.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Days can't be selected; the calendar only shows dates. |
| `Single` | One date at a time: a click replaces the selection (the default). |
| `Multiple` | Any number of dates: a click adds or removes one. |

### CalendarViewDisplayMode

```cpp
enum class CalendarViewDisplayMode
```

What a [CalendarView](#uicalendarview) shows.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Month` | The days of one month, six weeks at a time (the default). |
| `Year` | The months of one year. |
| `Decade` | The years of one decade. |
